record.original_question: Given a function kappa in C^-1(0,+infinity), what conditions are necessary and sufficient for kappa to belong to the class Ln of generalized Sonine-kernel pairs satisfying (kappa * k)(t) = 1^{<n>}(t), and how can one derive a representation of the associated kernel k?

evidence.quote: Definition 2 ([40]). Let the functions kappa and k satisfy the condition (45) and the inclusions kappa in C^-1(0, +infinity), k in C^-1,0(0, +infinity) hold true. The set of pairs (kappa, k) of such kernels will be denoted by Ln.
For a function kappa in C^-1(0, +infinity), determine the conditions for the inclusion kappa in Ln and derive a representation for the associated kernel k.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$ denote the space of functions $f:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $f(t)=t^{p}f_1(t)$ for some $p>-1$ and some $f_1\in C[0,+\infty)$, and let $C_{-1,0}(0,+\infty)$ denote the subspace of those with $p>-1$ allowing the exponent to range so that $f$ may be locally integrable but possibly singular at $0$. For $n\in\mathbb{N}$ let 
$$1^{\langle n\rangle}(t)=\frac{t^{n-1}}{(n-1)!},\qquad t>0,$$
and denote by $*$ the Laplace convolution $(f*g)(t)=\int_0^t f(t-\tau)g(\tau)\,d\tau$. Define the class $\mathcal{L}_n$ of generalized Sonine kernel pairs as the set of pairs $(\varkappa,k)$ with $\varkappa\in C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$, $k\in C_{-1,0}(0,+\infty)$ satisfying
$$(\varkappa * k)(t)=1^{\langle n\rangle}(t),\qquad t>0.$$

Problem: Given a function $\varkappa\in C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$, find necessary and sufficient conditions on $\varkappa$ for the existence of a kernel $k\in C_{-1,0}(0,+\infty)$ such that $(\varkappa,k)\in\mathcal{L}_n$, and provide an explicit representation formula for the associated kernel $k$ in terms of $\varkappa$.
artifact.category_tag: Generalized Sonine kernels and fractional calculus
artifact.status_search_result: A complete intrinsic characterization of $\mathcal{L}_n$ membership for arbitrary $\varkappa\in C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$, together with an explicit formula for the associated kernel $k$, does not appear to be established. Existing work characterizes pairs in $\mathcal{L}_n$ via Laplace transforms ($\widetilde\varkappa(p)\widetilde k(p)=1/p^n$) and constructs examples (power kernels, Bessel-type kernels, and pairs derived from $\mathcal{L}_1$ Sonine pairs), but it is also noted that such constructions do not exhaust $\mathcal{L}_n$. The problem of giving necessary and sufficient conditions plus a representation of $k$ appears to remain open in the general setting.

status_evidence.title: General Fractional Calculus: Multi-Kernel Approach
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes pairs in L_n via Laplace transforms and gives examples (power and Bessel-type kernels) but notes constructions from L_1 do not cover all of L_n.
status_evidence.claim: Membership in L_n is currently described via Laplace-transform identity and example constructions; no general intrinsic characterization for arbitrary kappa is given.

status_evidence.title: Extension of Luchko operational calculus to multi-Kernel general fractional derivatives
status_evidence.snippet: Builds operational calculus on Luchko's L_n classes, taking the membership conditions as a starting hypothesis rather than deriving an intrinsic characterization.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent works treat L_n as a postulated class, indicating the characterization question remains open.
